brief.topic: Why Seven Has Six Ways to Arrive

s01: Two fair dice do not make equally likely totals.
Every ordered pair is equally likely. There are thirty six pairs.
To total seven, the first die can be one and the second six.
Or two and five. Continue along this diagonal. Six different pairs work.
To total two, only one and one work. So seven is six times as likely as two.
Collect the pairs for every total. Their counts rise to six and fall again.
For independent dice, multiply the probabilities inside each pair, then add across pairs with the same sum.
This operation is convolution. It combines distributions when independent quantities are added.
Now use the same die twice: copy its result instead of rolling independently.
Each individual result is still uniform, but only matching pairs can occur.
The totals are two, four, six, eight, ten and twelve, each with probability one sixth. Seven is impossible. Same individual distributions, different dependence, different sum.

scenes.narration:
Two fair dice do not make equally likely totals. Every ordered pair is equally likely. There are thirty six pairs.

To total seven, the first die can be one and the second six. Or two and five. Continue along this diagonal. Six different pairs work. To total two, only one and one work. So seven is six times as likely as two.

Collect the pairs for every total. Their counts rise to six and fall again. For independent dice, multiply the probabilities inside each pair, then add across pairs with the same sum. This operation is convolution. It combines distributions when independent quantities are added.

Now use the same die twice: copy its result instead of rolling independently. Each individual result is still uniform, but only matching pairs can occur. The totals are two, four, six, eight, ten and twelve, each with probability one sixth. Seven is impossible. Same individual distributions, different dependence, different sum.
